events.title: U.S. Dollar Advances As Investors Analyze NFP Data Amid U.S.-Iran Stalemate
events.description: The U.S. Dollar value moved higher on Friday as the October nonfarm payrolls came in strongly above market forecasts while the unemployment rate slumped from September numbers. In addition, the U.S.-Iran conflict continues without an end in sight triggering inflation concerns.

events.title: Swiss Market Ends Notably Lower
events.description: The Switzerland stock market ended weak on Friday after remaining in negative territory throughout the session, amid a sell-off in global equity markets amid concerns about returns on AI-related investments.

events.title: European Stocks Tumble On AI Regulation Fears
events.description: European equities fell Friday as investors worried about potential AI regulation tightening under the Trump administration and reacted to corporate earnings and economic data releases across the region.

events.title: Canadian Market Up Firmly As Traders React To Jobs Data, Earnings
events.description:
The Canadian market gained modest ground in positive territory Friday morning, supported by gains in healthcare, technology, energy and materials sectors. Shares from other sectors turned in a mixed performance.

Stronger-than-expected U.S. non-farm payroll data aided sentiment.

events.title: U.S. Consumer Sentiment Unexpectedly Improves In November
events.description: Preliminary data released by the University of Michigan on Friday showed an unexpected improvement in U.S. consumer sentiment in the month of November. The University of Michigan said its consumer sentiment index rose to 51.0 in November from 48.0 in October. Economists had expected the index to remain unchanged.

events.title: U.S. Employment Jumps Much More Than Expected In October
events.description: A closely watched report released by the Labor Department on Friday showed employment in the U.S. increased by far more than anticipated in the month of October. The Labor Department said non-farm payroll employment jumped by 165,000 jobs in October compared to economist estimates for the addition of 62,000 jobs.

events.title: Bay Street May Open On Mixed Note, Reacting To Jobs Data, Earnings
events.description: Canadian stocks are likely to open on a mixed note on Friday. Tech stocks may rebound, tracking gains of leading US tech stocks in pre-market trades today. Investors will also react to Canadian and U.S. jobs data, and a slew of corporate earnings reports.

events.title: U.S. Employment Jumps Much More Than Expected In October
events.description: A closely watched report released by the Labor Department on Friday showed employment in the U.S. increased by far more than anticipated in the month of October.

events.title: Euro Falls After Weak Eurozone Retail Sales Data
events.description: The euro weakened against most major currencies in the European session on Friday, after Eurozone retail trade volume decreased in September after rebounding in the previous month.

events.title: Euro Falls Against Most Majors
events.description: The euro weakened against most major currencies in the European session on Friday.

events.title: Pound Falls As European Shares Traded Lower
events.description: The British pound weakened against other major currencies in the European session on Friday, as European shares fell sharply on Friday as the Democratic Party's sweeping wins at this week's midterm elections in the U.S. sparked fears of a slowdown in the pace of AI infrastructure development.

events.title: FTSE 100 Down 2.3% On Widespread Selling
events.description:
The U.K. stock market's benchmark index FTSE 100 fell to a four-week low Friday morning as a sell-off in global equity markets rendered the mood bearish right from the start. 

Uncertainty about the potential economic impact of the Democrats' sweeping win in the US midterm elections contributed to the reduced risk appetite in global markets.

events.title: CAC 40 Down Sharply On Weak Global Cues
events.description: France's equity benchmark CAC 40 dropped sharply Friday morning amid rising concerns the Democratic Party's sweeping wins in the US midterm elections could result in tighter regulation of the AI industry and slowdown in data center expansion.
